🚑 Account Rescue: When Things Go Wrong · Lesson 1 of 6

Hacked: The First 60 Minutes and the Official Way Back In

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

Telegram gives you a 24-hour head start against a hacker. A device that has just logged in can't kick out older sessions for its first 24 hours. If you act inside that window, your own phone can throw the intruder out.

Every platform has small rules like that, and they decide who wins the race for your account. Here's the first-hour plan, the official route for each app, and what to tell followers while you get back in.

9 months
how far back YouTube's support can help with a hacked channel. Older incidents may not be recoverable because of data retention (YouTube Help: Recover a hacked channel)

The first 60 minutes, in order

  1. Check your phone signal. 'No service' where you normally have network can mean a SIM swap. From another phone, call Safaricom on 100 (prepaid) or 200 (postpaid), or +254 722 002 100 from any network. Airtel: 100 from an Airtel line or 0733 100 100 from other networks.
  2. Rescue your email first. Every other account resets through it. For Gmail, use accounts.google.com/signin/recovery.
  3. Start the official recovery route for the hacked app (table below). Meta says its recovery now checks trusted devices and past login locations, so try from the phone and Wi-Fi you normally use.
  4. Once you're in, lock the doors. Change the password, log out every other session, remove any email or phone number you don't recognise, and turn 2FA on.
  5. Undo the damage fast. Delete posts the hacker made, fix your bio link, and check payout details. YouTube says quick clean-up can help you avoid strikes for content you didn't post.
  6. Warn your followers from a channel you still control (template below).
  7. Screenshot everything: security emails, times and messages. You'll need it for appeals and any police report.

The official route for each platform

PlatformWhere to startKnow this
Instagraminstagram.com/hackedCovers hacked accounts, forgotten passwords and lost 2FA access. An optional video selfie may be offered.
Facebookfacebook.com/hackedReport the account as compromised even if you can still log in.
TikTokLogin screen > Report a problemHave your old email or phone, the devices you used and screenshots ready as proof.
YouTubeRecover the Google Account first, then the hacked-channel assistant: support.google.com/youtube/?p=ytRecoveryCawfPartner Program creators can contact Creator Support once the Google Account is back. Others can try @TeamYouTube on X.
X'Forgot password', then a Support Request from the account's emailInclude your username and the date you last had access.
TelegramSettings > Devices > Terminate all other sessionsLocked out? Use telegram.org/support or Settings > Ask a question. Nowhere else.
WhatsAppRe-register your number with the 6-digit codeThis logs out every other device. If a PIN you don't know appears, a recovery email resets it; without one you wait 7 days.
EndaViralOpen a support ticket with your order IDDo this if an order was delivering to the account when it was hijacked or renamed.
💡 What most people miss about the video selfie

Meta's optional video selfie is compared against photos already on the account, and Meta says the facial data is deleted after the check. If your profile has never shown your face, there may be nothing to match. Then you'll need another route, like ID or a recovery email.

✗ MYTH

Once I reset the password, the hacker is out.

✓ REALITY

Not always. Sessions that are already logged in can stay alive, and hackers often add their own email, phone or 2FA so they can come back. After a reset, log out all other sessions and check every recovery detail and connected app.

Recovery is free. 'Recovery agents' are not

In June 2026 KrebsOnSecurity reported attackers tricking Meta's AI support chat into adding their email to Instagram accounts. Meta said it was fixed, and the hackers said it failed on accounts with 2FA on. Use only official routes. Anyone who DMs offering to 'recover' your account for a fee is a second scam.

📋 Follower warning (post on WhatsApp Status or another account)
Heads up: my [Instagram/TikTok] account @[handle] was hacked on [date]. I'm recovering it through the official [Instagram/TikTok] process.
Until I confirm here that it's fixed:
- I am NOT selling anything, running giveaways or asking for M-Pesa.
- Don't click links or send any code that account asks for.
- If it DMs you for money, report it and block.
Please share so nobody gets conned. - [Your name]
✅ Do this today (even if you're not hacked)
⚡ Quick check

A stranger logged into your Telegram on a new phone 3 hours ago. You're still logged in on yours. What should you do right now?

A new device can't end your older session for its first 24 hours, but your phone can end its session. After 24 hours the hacker can lock you out, so act inside that window.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Phone signal and email come first. A SIM swap or lost inbox unlocks everything else.
  2. Use only official routes like instagram.com/hacked, facebook.com/hacked and Google account recovery.
  3. After getting back in, end every session and remove the hacker's email, phone and 2FA.
  4. Warn followers from a channel you control, and screenshot everything.
